Theme

phrase noun

a group of words, an expression

also phrases, expression, set phrase, turn of phrase, phrasing

classical

Gell. 1.7.18: locūtiōnum tālium cōpiam
Traupman 248

locūtiō, locūtiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a phrase, an expression

Properly a speaking, and in Cicero a way of speaking: ēmendāta et Latīna locūtiō (Brut. 258). The sense “phrase, expression” is post-Augustan (Gellius); in Quintilian 1.5.2 it is even a single word (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • verba, verbōrum n. pl. — words; the wording

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical

    The everyday way: hīs verbīs, in these words; ad verbum, word for word (Cic. Fin. 1.4).

  • fōrmula, fōrmulae f. — a set form of words

    noun, first declension · also used · classical

    A fixed form, chiefly of law and ritual (testāmentōrum fōrmulae, Cic.), so a set phrase; also a rule or method (Lewis & Short).

  • dictiō, dictiōnis f. — a way of putting it, an expression

    noun, third declension · also used · classical

    Classically a speaking or pleading, a style of delivery; “the use of a word or phrase” in Quintilian and Gellius, and a single word in the grammarians (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • multam nōs quoque apud veterēs scrīptōrēs locūtiōnum tālium cōpiam offendimus

    we too have come upon a great many phrases of that kind in the old writersGell. 1.7.18

See also word, sentence, quote.

SourcesLewis & Short: locutio · Lewis & Short: verbum · Lewis & Short: formula · Lewis & Short: dictio
